header.name: Knowledge Production, Concepts and Context
header.description: This course will enable students to grasp the nature of knowledge in humanities and social sciences. They will learn about the way concepts are developed and also the way they can misinform if not formulated with a deeper understanding of historical and social contexts. The course aims to expose students to advanced debates around concept formation and epistemology in social sciences and humanities which can enable them to interpret critical texts and situate them within relevant socio-historical philosophical and methodological contexts. It will also enable students to critically examine the conceptual claims made in the text and require students to apply them to their own research and disciplinary contexts. Designed primarily for graduate students, the course will be run in a seminar format, wherein a cluster of classes will be led by an instructor. The classes will enable a deep reading of the selected material and will form the basis of their dissertation projects. specific texts will be decided by the course instructor and may vary across different semesters.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to grasp the nature of knowledge in social sciences, with a reference to the relationship between philosophy, theory and history

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to interpret critical texts in their socio-historical, philosophical context and develop methodological approaches to undertake independent research projects

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to apply relevant concepts in their own research.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to demonstrate clarity, precision, and accuracy in reasoning and avoid fallacies

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: the students will be able to relate to the text as both a site of thought and a tradition of thinking about issues of the world and gather insights about contemporary concerns
